Definition: from G5007; talent-like in weight:--weight of a talent.
BiblicalUsage: John says a great hail out of heaven fell upon men, every stone about the weight of a talent. The word means talent-like in weight, as heavy as the largest measure. It is the last plague's picture: judgment falling from the sky, and men blaspheming God because of it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the weight of the hail is the point: judgment is not light, and the hardness of heart that curses through it is the saddest part of the verse.
